Officer's narrative
On arrival at the intersection in Pasadena, Texas, I found a side-impact collision between two passenger vehicles.
Driver 1 was operating a sedan that had entered the intersection when Driver 2's vehicle struck its driver's side. Driver
1 is the individual listed on the policy for the sedan. A Passenger was seated in the vehicle at the time.
Driver 1 reported pain in the right shoulder. The nature of the impact, with the force directed into the side of the cab, is
consistent with the injury described. Driver 2 stated that the collision happened as Driver 1 described it, and two
independent witnesses gave accounts that agree with both drivers' versions. Scene photographs show damage
concentrated on the driver's side of Driver 1's vehicle and on the front quarter of Driver 2's vehicle, which fits the
reported angle of impact.
I found no indication of prior damage to either vehicle. It was not fully clear from the scene where in the vehicle Driver
1 was seated at the moment of impact, and this will need to be confirmed in follow-up interviews. Both vehicles were
towed from the scene.
</page>
